name: Starker
label: RRR Music Group
lede: Starker draws a cartoon dog for Westside Gunn, owns Polo pieces the company's own offices lack, and in 2026 takes an 8.4 from Pitchfork for a 32-minute tape about a Brooklyn that's mostly gone.

eras.title: Two dudes from audio school
eras.text: Starker and YL meet in an engineering class, bond over Rawkus compilations and Max B freestyles, and put out a tape that finds its first audience overseas.

years.h: A classmate introduces Starker to YL at audio school
years.p: The Institute of Audio Research, 2014. They turn out to own the same canon: the Rawkus Soundbombing comps and [[Max B|372119b0-2350-455f-acd8-6371bc947531]] freestyles.
years.xp:
YL told The FADER he had never met anyone "this much into the same shit I was", and that Starker kept putting him on, too.

The origin story of their crew, RRR Music Group (Real Recognize Real), depends on who tells it. The FADER has YL starting the label in 2010. Bandcamp Daily has it beginning as high-school "homie shit", with a member called MID the first to rap and YL the videographer, and Starker inducted in 2015.

eras.title: The tape people still point to
eras.text: Starker and YL's first project. A decade later, people still point to it as where the whole thing starts.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily · The Harvard Crimson · Orbit
years.h: Lo.Ceasar sets a gruff voice against a laid-back one
years.p: Starker's aggressive growl, YL's easygoing delivery. On the cover YL wears the North Face Nuptse jacket that became his look.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily quotes YL on the pairing: Starker's gruff timbre is the counterpoint to his own lackadaisical flow. The Harvard Crimson credits it as the earliest project Starker released, and the Substack profile Orbit dates his public rise to it and its single "Lo Ceasar".

Its reach went past Brooklyn. YL credited the tape's impact in Japan for making a later trip possible.

eras.title: Treated like an artist
eras.text: Japan turns out to be the first place that books Starker as a performer. The duo keep returning, and the tape gets a Japanese CD.

years.big: "I went to Japan and got treated like an artist for the first time in my life."
years.p: Starker's words to The Harvard Crimson on his first solo show, in Morioka, nearly a decade into making music. The mother of his child bought the ticket as a Valentine's Day gift.
years.xp: The Crimson describes the 2017 trip as a turning point. It was the first time he performed a solo set, and it restored his confidence and his output.

years.h: YL, Starker and MID fly to Japan and record Made in Japan
years.p: Starker's connections there made the trip possible. A Japanese CD of Lo.Ceasar follows the same year.
years.xp:
YL told Bandcamp Daily the trip was possible because of Starker's earlier connections and the response to Lo.Ceasar.

The CD, Lo.Ceasar Special Edition, came out in 2018 on RRR Music Group as catalog number SC-0001. Per Discogs it has 19 tracks, with beats by Wun Two, Central Parks and others.

years.h: Knuckleheads gets pitched as rap's Darius Miles and Quentin Richardson
years.p: The Modern Life covers the EP in October and frames the pair as the hip-hop version of the Clippers duo.

eras.title: Brands call, and a cartoon dog lands on a Gunn cover
eras.text: Brands notice a rapper who knows their archives better than they do. Meanwhile the tapes keep coming, the art gets noticed, and RRR puts out its first full album.

years.cap: Starker with his Polo Ralph Lauren collection
years.src: Highsnobiety · The Harvard Crimson · Fresh NewSnow
yt: YL, Starker and Zoomo interview with Fresh News Now
years.h: Aimé Leon Dore puts Starker in a New Balance campaign
years.p: Highsnobiety later picks him as the American face of Polo Ralph Lauren's Superfans series, as a vintage Polo collector.
years.xp:
Highsnobiety's July 2022 Superfans piece shows off his apartment: a 1993 Climb rugby shirt, pieces from Polo's 1992 Stadium and 1993 Snow Beach lines, windbreakers and caps. The Crimson reports his collection includes items even Polo's corporate offices lack.

His line in that piece: "Polo will always be timeless because Polo's a part of inner-city New York culture."

On July 10, 2021, RRR (Starker, YL, Zoomo) played Lot 45 in Brooklyn, and Starker told Fresh NewSnow the first second of the set felt "really locked in".

years.h: LO.FACE returns with a two-word note: WE BACK
years.p: That's the entire description on the Bandcamp page. The tape runs 16 tracks, and closer "EPCOT" is a bonus.

years.h: Starker draws the cover for Westside Gunn's Peace "Fly" God
years.p: His signature is a cartoon dog modeled on Betty Boop's Bimbo, per the Crimson. He had drawn al.divino's Secrets in 2020.

yt: YL & Starker live at Elsewhere, Brooklyn: "Gilbert Arenas", "Allergic to Broke" (2023)
years.h: RRR: The Album is the label's first full record
years.p: YL, Starker and producer Zoomo, 14 tracks, including "Gilbert Arenas" and "Allergic to Broke".

eras.title: North Face Nace
eras.text: A double act's 2024 album gets a listening party at Aimé Leon Dore, and two years later Starker's own tape lands a Pitchfork 8.4.

years.cap: YL (back to camera) and Starker by a red Jeep in Brooklyn, 2024
years.src: Album of the Year · The FADER
years.h: YL and Starker name Diamond Collection after game-worn MLB gear
years.p: Seventeen tracks, titled for the vintage baseball apparel they collect. Producers include Zoomo, Noface, Subjxct 5 and Lord Unknown.
years.xp:
The FADER reports it took a year of regular studio sessions and was one of their few records with producers beyond the in-house pair, Zoomo and Noface. The release party was held at Aimé Leon Dore's private sound room, with co-signs from Eyedress and [[Westside Gunn|9f42ba3d-3cfc-499c-ba16-7226f56b622f]].

Starker on why the record matters to him: "Every block, every business, just opens and closes so fast."

years.cap: Starker outside Gage & Tolner in Downtown Brooklyn, 2026
years.src: Album of the Year · Bandcamp: Starker
years.h: Pitchfork gives LIVING TYPE DANGEROUS Vol. 1 an 8.4
years.p: Alphonse Pierre's review covers 19 tracks in 32 minutes. Nicholas Craven produces the most, with YL and Goya Gumbani among the guests.
years.xp:
Album of the Year lists Pitchfork's summary of the tape as "Retro but never dusty", a "brilliantly bugged-out" record that sounds like "a New York that hardly exists anymore." Producers include Craven, Laron, Benji Socrate$, Lord Unknown and Foule Monk. Closer "Ronda" is a bonus track.

Starker's own Bandcamp caption calls it "BIG BROOKLYN BIG LTD SHIT!" The title plays on his own name and the North Face jackets that run through the RRR look.

years.cap: Starker in the tiki bar above a steakhouse in Downtown Brooklyn, 2026
yt: Starker - Banned From JPN (Prod. Nicholas Craven)
years.h: Two Nicholas Craven beats, "Banned From JPN" and "Van Sons", get videos
years.p: Insomniac lists those two, plus "Questlove" and "Civil War", as highlights of the tape.

sources.title: Album of the Year: Starker, LIVING TYPE DANGEROUS Vol. 1
